newsitem.title: USA: Houston Ship Channel reopens to deep-draft traffic.
newsitem.headline: Houston Ship Channel reopens to deep-draft traffic.

text.p: The Houston Ship Channel, a key waterway used by tankers to reach area refineries, was reopened to deep-draft traffic Friday as a heavy fog lifted, the Houston Pilots Association said.
Pilots began sailing outbound ships at 0900 CST/1500 GMT, and were en route to Galveston to board the first of 33 inbound ships delayed by the heavy fog, a dispatcher said.
"Pilots are en route to Galveston now to board inbounds," the dispatcher said.
Unseasonably warm weather has shrouded the channel in dense morning fog over the past several days, delaying ships sailing for area refineries, chemical plants and the Port of Houston.
The Houston Ship Channel connects the Port of Houston to Galveston Bay and the Gulf of Mexico.
